content: 1. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of nateglinide due to competition for plasma protein binding. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 2. Nitisinone increases the levels or effects of sulfadiazine by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Nitisinone is a CYP2C9 inhibitor, so co-administration with CYP2C9 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index, requires caution. 3. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of ospemifene by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Sulfadiazine and porfimer exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced photosensitivity. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Promazine increases the toxicity of sulfadiazine through an unspecified interaction mechanism, potentially enhancing myelosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of repaglinide due to competition for plasma protein binding. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of sulfadiazine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Dosage adjustments of CYP2C9 substrates may be necessary if clinically indicated. 8. Sulfadiazine decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Co-administration with antibiotics reduces efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora required for sodium picosulfate activation. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of sulfadiazine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Sparsentan, a CYP2C9 inducer, reduces exposure to CYP2C9 substrates and their efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Sulfadiazine increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Co-administration of sulfadiazine and tetracaine may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia. Monitor for signs of methemoglobinemia when using methemoglobin-inducing drugs together. 12. Sulfadiazine and valoctocogene roxaparvovec may both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Medications that cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec may elevate liver enzyme levels. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications to avoid potential drug interactions. 13. Co-administration of sulfadiazine and voclosporin may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute or chronic nephrotoxicity when used together. 14. Sulfadiazine increases the levels or effects of warfarin by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism and displacing protein binding. Consider reducing the warfarin dose by 10-20% if co-administered. Monitor therapy closely. 15. Amiloride increases the levels of sulfadiazine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 16. Sulfadiazine interferes with the chemical color development of aminohippurate (PAH), which is essential for accurate renal clearance analysis. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Aspirin increases the levels of sulfadiazine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 18. Sulfadiazine decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 19. Bumetanide increases the levels of sulfadiazine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 20. Sulfadiazine decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of phenytoin by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Sulfadiazine and primaquine exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency. The clinical significance is unknown. 23. Probenecid increases the levels of sulfadiazine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 24. Sulfadiazine decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 25. Sulfadiazine and pyrimethamine exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing bone marrow toxicity. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of antithrombin alfa by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of antithrombin III by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of sulfadiazine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if co-administration is necessary. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of argatroban by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Sulfadiazine decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. 31. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of bemiparin by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Sulfadiazine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Sulfadiazine decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as they may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 34. Cannabidiol increases the levels or effects of sulfadiazine by inhibiting CYP2C9 activity. Consider reducing the dose of sulfadiazine when co-administered. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 35. Sulfadiazine decreases the effects of cyclosporine through an unknown mechanism. Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely.
